text:
maya: quick follow-up on the prefill/warmup shaping experiment I ran on canary (node pool B). wanted to capture results + a small heuristic we can try before any big refactor.

kevin: tl;dr — good perf wins for mixed workloads. overall p95 token latency down ~7%, cost/token ~3% lower when we bias prefill to hot prefixes.

sasha: can you explain "bias prefill to hot prefixes" in one sentence? worried about hot-tenant domination of warmup budget.

maya: sure — rather than prefill uniformly for every new sequence, we score prefixes by recent hit-rate and avg seqlen and allocate warmup budget proportionally. effectively prefer prefill on prefixes that historically reduce subsequent decode work.

chris: sketch of the scoring we used: score = hit_rate * log(1 + avg_seqlen) * (1 - recent_eviction_penalty). old naive: allocate equal budget to all tenants. new: budget ~ softmax(scores) * global_budget.

kevin: config we toggled on canary (copy):
```yaml
prefill_warmup:
  enabled: true
  global_budget_tokens_per_sec: 20000
  tenant_budget_fraction_cap: 0.1
  prefix_score:
    smoothing_window_secs: 300
    seqlen_floor: 16
    penalty_decay_secs: 600
```

sasha: hmm tenant_budget_fraction_cap helps. what's eviction order when cache is full? lru?

maya: eviction is still LRU for now but we add a small "prefill_affinity" tag so prefills try to colocate in same cache region (so you don't evict your own useful kvs immediately).

chris: implementation note: prefer soft affinity to avoid long-lived fragmentation. we use an affinity score that decays exponentially: affinity = exp(-age_sec / 120).

elin: what metrics did you capture so we can decide rollout? put these on the dashboard pls: warmup_prefill_hit_rate, warmup_eviction_count, avg_prefill_latency, token_cost_delta_by_tenant.

kevin: logs snippet from canary (sanitized):
```
[2024-11-08 10:12:34] tenant=acme warmup_alloc=512 tokens prefill=35 hit_after=0.68 eviction=1
[2024-11-08 10:12:45] tenant=beta warmup_alloc=128 tokens prefill=12 hit_after=0.12 eviction=0
```

maya: interesting signal: acme had high hit_after and helped downstream latency; beta didn't — suggests we should gate by per-tenant hit_rate threshold before giving sustained budget.

chris: proposed quick heuristic to avoid refactor: two-stage gating:
1) trial allocation: give a small trial_prefill (e.g., 16 tokens) when seqlen > seqlen_threshold. measure hit_after within window.
2) promote to steady budget only if trial_hit_rate > 0.25 and avg_seqlen > 64.

kevin: +1, easy kill-switch. we can also add a CPU guard so warmup doesn't starve CPU on smaller machines.

ops-bot: deploy successful: flag prefill_warmup.enabled=true on canary cluster (pool B) at rev r-20241108-9.

maya: next steps: 1) put the metrics on runtime dashboard (elin), 2) add the trial->promote gating and tenant cap (kevin/chris), 3) run 2-week canary and collect per-tenant cost deltas (maya).

kevin: i'll open a tiny RFC addendum summarizing the heuristic and the config knobs. will link to thread.

maya: thanks all. @sasha @elin please poke if you see weird tenant regressions. :eyes:
